contentFuel.author: AndrewYNg
contentFuel.content:
New course: Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents, built in partnership with @jetbrains, and taught by @paulweveritt.

Vibe coding is fast, but often produces code that doesn't match what you asked for. This short course teaches you spec-driven development: write a detailed spec defining what to build, and work with your coding agent to implement it. Many of the best developers already build this way.

A spec lets you control large code changes with a few words, preserve context across agen
contentFuel.whyKeep: Andrew Ng course on spec-driven development: write detailed specs before coding with agents — directly teachable workflow for anyone using AI coding tools

contentFuel.author: bcherny
contentFuel.content:
6/ Give Claude a way to verify its work

Finally, make sure Claude has a way to verify its work. This has always been a way to 2-3x what you get out of Claude, and with 4.7 it's more important than ever.

Verification looks different depending on the task. For backend work, make sure Claude knows how to start up your server/service to test it end to end; for frontend work, use the Claude Chromium extension to give Claude a way to control your browser; for desktop apps, use computer use.

Persona
contentFuel.whyKeep: Boris Cherny's concrete tip: give Claude verification methods (start server for backend, Chromium for frontend) to 2-3x output quality

contentFuel.author: startupideaspod
contentFuel.content:
Here's how to go from "looks AI-generated" to "who designed this?":

Step 1: Screenshot sites you admire 

Drop them into Claude. 

Say "extrapolate the key design elements and create a design system."

Step 2: Save that style guide 

Every future component references it. 

That's how you get consistency.

Step 3: Use existing component libraries as reference 

Tools like Tailarc Pro give you polished blocks and illustrations to build on top of.

Step 4: Refine in Figma/paper first 

Try differe
contentFuel.whyKeep: Exact 3-step process: screenshot sites → prompt Claude to extract design system → use component libraries for consistent AI-generated designs.

contentFuel.author: startupideaspod
contentFuel.content:
Most people prompt every AI video model the same way.

That's why their results are inconsistent.

Here's what actually works:

Kling 3: 
- Rewards brevity Short
- Simple prompts with fewer tokens tend to produce better output. 
- Less is more.

Seedance 2.0: 
- Rewards extreme specificity 
- The more detail you give, the better it performs 
- Especially for preserving character identity, motion, and transitions across scenes.

Source reference image: The multiplier 
- Before any prompt, feed it
contentFuel.whyKeep: Specific prompting strategies per video model: Kling 3 rewards brevity, Seedance 2.0 rewards extreme specificity — actionable differences.

contentFuel.author: bcherny
contentFuel.content:
5/ Configure your effort level

Opus 4.7 uses adaptive thinking instead of thinking budgets. To tune the model to think more/less, we recommend tuning effort.

Use lower effort for faster responses and lower token usage. Use higher effort for the most intelligence and capability.

Personally, I use xhigh effort for most tasks, and max effort for the hardest tasks. Max applies to just your current session; other effort levels are sticky and persist for your next session also.

/effort to set your
contentFuel.whyKeep: Specific Claude Code CLI configuration tip: how to tune effort levels (xhigh vs max) for different task complexities.

contentFuel.author: bcherny
contentFuel.content:
4/ Focus mode

I've been loving the new focus mode in the CLI, which hides all the intermediate work to just focus on the final result. The model has reached a point where I generally  trust it to run the right commands and make the right edits. I just look at the final result.

/focus to toggle on/off.
contentFuel.whyKeep: Specific Claude Code CLI feature: /focus command to hide intermediate work and only see final results.

emerging.signal: OpenAI is carving out domain-specific frontier models starting with biology — this signals the end of 'one model fits all' and the beginning of vertical model wars where pharma budgets justify dedicated training runs.

Google skipped the demo phase and went straight to embodied reasoning on commercial hardware — this is the clearest signal yet that foundation models are ready to leave the screen and enter physical operations.

Cloudflare shipping both inference and email primitives purpose-built for agents means the 'agent cloud' is becoming a real infrastructure category — the middleware tax on agentic apps just found its toll booth.

consolidating.signal: Every single day has multiple items on Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, or spec-driven development — the developer role is actively mutating from 'writes code' to 'reviews and orchestrates AI output', and the Jevons paradox data proves demand increases, not decreases.

Opus 4.7 dominated two consecutive days across Anthropic, Cursor, and independent devs — adaptive effort levels and async work are shifting the conversation from 'is it smart enough' to 'how autonomously should we let it run'.

LangChain shipping three tiers (create-agent, deepagents, middleware), OpenAI expanding Agents SDK, CrewAI calling it all furniture rearrangement — the agentic framework layer is commoditizing fast, and the real moat is moving to eval loops and memory, not orchestration.
